input: Review and update my life insurance beneficiaries

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may have one policy or several (employer-provided, individual, term, whole life) — knowing how many and what types determines the full scope of the review.
Understanding who the current beneficiaries are and who the user wants to add, remove, or change determines what updates actually need to be made.
A life event (marriage, divorce, new child, death of a beneficiary) is often the trigger — knowing this shapes the urgency and specific changes needed.
Whether the user knows how to access their policy documents and insurer portal — or needs guidance locating them — determines the very first action step.
Some policies require notarized forms, spousal consent, or have processing windows — knowing if there is a deadline or legal requirement affects how to sequence the task.
The user may want a simple primary beneficiary update, or a more thorough setup with contingent beneficiaries and specific percentage splits — this affects depth of the plan.
The user may consider this done when the form is submitted, or only when written confirmation from the insurer is received — this defines the finish line.

gold.taskTitle: Review and update life insurance beneficiaries
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to review who is currently named as beneficiaries on their life insurance policy and make any necessary updates to those designations.

questions.title: How many life insurance policies do you currently have?
questions.description: Identify whether this covers one policy or multiple (e.g., employer group plan, individual term, whole life) to determine the full scope of the review.

questions.title: What life event is prompting this review right now?
questions.description: Understand the trigger (e.g., marriage, divorce, new child, death of a beneficiary, or just routine review) to clarify what specific changes are needed.

questions.title: Who do you want named as your beneficiaries going forward?
questions.description: Establish the target beneficiary lineup — names, relationships, and whether one person or multiple people are involved — to define exactly what needs updating.

questions.title: Do you want contingent beneficiaries and percentage splits set up?
questions.description: Determine the desired depth of the designation — a single primary beneficiary vs. a structured setup with backups and allocated percentages.

questions.title: Do you already have access to your insurer's portal or paper forms?
questions.description: Find out if the user knows where to get the change-of-beneficiary form or log in to their insurer's system, which determines the immediate first action.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or legal requirement you are working against?
questions.description: Identify any time pressure, such as an open enrollment window, court order, divorce decree, or spousal consent requirement, that would affect how quickly and carefully this must be done.

questions.title: What would make you feel this task is fully complete?
questions.description: Clarify the finish line — whether it is submitting the form, receiving written confirmation from the insurer, or verifying the change appears on the policy documents.
